newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Wing Tiek reports loss on Filipino deal.
newsitem.headline: Wing Tiek reports loss on Filipino deal.

text.p: Malaysian industrial group Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd said on Friday it made a loss of 146 million ringgit after the sale of two Philippines companies.
Wing Tiek said in a statement the losses were incurred by the sale of Philippine steel firm, National Steel Corp, and holding company, Wing Tiek Holdings Asia, Inc (WTHAI).

"The disposal of National Steel Corporation (NSC) and WTHAI have resulted in a loss of 146 million ringgit to the group, which is 43 million over and above the estimated loss of 103 million ringgit made known to the shareholders at the EGM (extraordinary meeting) on February 4, 1997," Wing Tiek said.
It said shareholders were told then that the full extent of the loss from the NSC sale could only be ascertained at a later date.
"The additional loss was due substantially to foreign exchange losses, additional interest, documentary stamp duties and Bureau of Inland Revenue charges," the statement said.
Wing Tiek said it has disposed of its entire shareholding of 12,500 shares in WTHAI to Westmont Holdings Sdn Bhd for 125,000 ringgit.
The disposal was also on condition that Westmont will assume a 77.7 million ringgit payment of advances due from WTHAI to Wing Tiek by July 31 this year.
The formerly state-owned NSC was acquired by Wing Tiek last year, but has since been sold to Hong Kong-based Hottic Investments Ltd for $800 million.
Hottic is a trust and investment company majority-owned by Malaysian businessmen led by Abdul Rashid bin Abdul Manaff.
Wing Tiek on Friday reported net profit of 1.22 million ringgit for the six-month period to January 31, down 84.57 percent from 4.26 million in the same period a year ago.
